tl;dr: who do you read/watch when you want to know if a movie has substance?

Your friends might tell you one thing or another, but if you press them for reasons, you might realize your friends are clueless, inarticulate, incurious, and will reliably skip seeing *The Shawshank Redemption* for the first time to re-watch some big-tittied waifu anime. This is why we have professionals.

I conditionally like Roger Ebert. He gives simple, populist answers to the question "is this movie worth seeing?" while also being conversant with the history and vocabulary of film. He grabs a movie by the handle by which it was meant to be taken, be it action, drama, or teen sex romp, and judges it on its own terms. I dig that. Being a critic. or a student of humanity requires seeing beyond one's own nose. I forgive him his occasional trespasses, like how he [excoriated Jurassic Park](http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/jurassic-park-1993), and his occasional fits of regressive-leftist scolding about gender roles and inclusion. I resent him more for having died three years ago, which has had a marked reduction on the quantity of his output.

I read maybe 40 reviews tonight, as I had made a small project of collecting a list of the 431 "best" movies of the current millennium. I'm done being completely out of touch with the last ten years, and with assuming that "there are no more classics." Bull shit! Tonight I learned about, like, *twenty.*

("2012" . "Cloud Atlas") ("2012" . "Looper") ("2012" . "Skyfall") ("2012" . "Savages") ("2006" . "The Prestige") ("2006" . "Casino Royale") ("2007" . "No Country for Old Men") ("2007" . "There Will Be Blood") ("2007" . "3:10 to Yuma") ("2008" . "The Dark Knight") ("2007" . "Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street") ("2003" . "Mystic River") ("2004" . "Sideways") ("2004" . "Kill Bill Vol. 2") ("2004" . "Million Dollar Baby") ("2008" . "WALL-E") ("2009" . "Inglourious Basterds") ("2009" . "Watchmen") ("2013" . "The Wolverine") ("2013" . "American Hustle") http://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/das-boot-1997 ("2004" . "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind") The Majestic ("2002" . "Catch Me If You Can")

Of course, 20 out of 40 being somewhere between "excellent" and "superlative" is an improbably high ratio, but you can surmise that I went after the titles that people never shut the fuck up about.

At this point I'm ready to hear some different voices weigh in on the remaining 390 movies... But *who?*
